insights.headline: MCX gold hits Rs 1,44,400 as softer oil and a weaker dollar lift bullion; silver up Rs 4,000
insights.summary: MCX December gold touched Rs 1,44,400 per 10 g and silver rose Rs 4,000 to Rs 1,88,979 per kg on Monday as softer oil eased inflation worries and the dollar softened; spot gold rose 1.6% to $4,129.69 and silver 2.8% to $53.31, with COMEX December gold up to $4,143.30. Dhanteras gold sales are estimated above Rs 62,000 crore, and traders await US October CPI on Tuesday, the next test for December Fed hike bets.
points: MCX December gold hit Rs 1,44,400 per 10 g on Monday, up about Rs 1,400 from Friday's close, as oil fell and the dollar eased.
Silver rose Rs 4,000 to Rs 1,88,979 per kg on MCX, while spot silver climbed 2.8% to $53.31 an ounce.
COMEX December gold climbed as much as $68.40 to $4,143.30 an ounce as crude fell after Trump said further Iran strikes were highly unlikely.
Dhanteras gold sales are estimated above Rs 62,000 crore, with festive demand staying firm despite elevated prices.
Traders await US October CPI on Tuesday, the next test for December Fed hike expectations after strong US jobs data.

brief.headline: Gold steady near Rs 1.44 lakh as oil eases; CPI next
brief.summary: MCX gold touched Rs 1,44,400 per 10 g and silver Rs 1,88,979 per kg as softer oil and a weaker dollar lifted bullion.

bullets.text: Softer oil after Trump said further Iran strikes were highly unlikely eased inflation worries, and a weaker dollar also lifted bullion.
Dhanteras sales are estimated above Rs 62,000 crore, while the rupee snapped a six-session winning streak on state banks' dollar bids.
US October CPI is due Tuesday at 19:00 IST, with PPI on Friday and a busy slate of Fed speeches through the week.

trending.title: Gold's Monday rebound
trending.summary: Softer oil and a weaker dollar lifted spot gold 1.6% to $4,129.69 on Monday, with silver up 2.8% to $53.31, extending last week's gains.

trending.title: US CPI is Tuesday's big test
trending.summary: Strong US jobs data has kept December Fed hike bets in focus, and Tuesday's October CPI is the next test for gold; a hot print could lift the dollar and yields.

trending.title: Dhanteras demand tops Rs 60,000 crore
trending.summary: Festive gold sales beat last year by value even as buyers chose lighter jewellery and smaller coins.

trending.title: Silver outpaces gold into the week
trending.summary: Silver rose 2.8% to $53.31 on Monday after a 5.75% weekly gain, with traders watching Tuesday's CPI and the $48 support zone.

trending.title: Banks split on gold's 2027 path
trending.summary: JPMorgan sees $6,300 an ounce in 2027 while other banks see $5,200-$5,250, and near-term forecasts put gold near $4,150 with MCX ranges of Rs 1,38,000-1,49,400.

items.title: MCX gold prices rise Rs 1,400/10g; silver up Rs 4,000/kg as fall in oil ease rate hike bets
items.summary: MCX December gold rose Rs 1,400 to Rs 1,43,933 per 10 g and silver gained Rs 4,000 to Rs 1,88,979 per kg on Monday, as falling crude oil eased inflation worries and cooled rate-hike bets while a weaker dollar supported bullion. Spot gold climbed 1.6% to $4,129.69 and silver 2.8% to $53.31; traders now await US CPI on Tuesday, with CME FedWatch pricing a 79% chance of a December Fed hike.

items.title: Gold Prices Rise Over One Per Cent As Lower Oil Prices Ease Inflation Concerns; US CPI Data In Focus
items.summary: MCX December gold gained 1.29% to Rs 1,44,400 per 10 g on Monday as falling crude eased inflation worries, with COMEX December gold up as much as $68.40 to $4,143.30 an ounce. Brent crude traded near $97.39 after the US president said further strikes on Iran were highly unlikely. Traders await US CPI on Tuesday, with CME FedWatch pricing an 81% chance of a December Fed hike.

items.title: Gold gains more than 1% as softer oil prices ease inflation worries
items.summary: Spot gold climbed 1.6% to $4,129.69 an ounce on Monday and December futures rose 1.6% to $4,139, as softer oil prices eased inflation worries. Oil fell after Trump said further attacks on Iran were highly unlikely while talks continue, and the dollar softened. Traders see a 79% chance of a December Fed hike; US CPI is due Tuesday and PPI on Friday. Silver rose 2.8% to $53.31.

items.title: Gold, silver prices rise up to 2.6% on COMEX; what investors are watching this week
items.summary: COMEX gold rose 1.45% to $4,134.10 an ounce on Monday and silver 2.63% to $53.31, extending last week's gains of 4.5% and 5.4%. MCX December gold gained about 3% on the week to Rs 1.42 lakh per 10 g and silver 3.15% to Rs 1.84 lakh per kg. Traders cited safe-haven demand, short-covering and are watching US-Iran developments and inflation data; MCX is shut Tuesday morning for Diwali-Balipratipada.

The US releases October CPI on Tuesday at 8:30 am ET, with economists expecting headline inflation up 0.24% on the month, down from 0.6% in September, and core CPI up 0.2%. The report is the key data point ahead of the Fed's December decision: a hotter print could lift the dollar and yields and pressure gold, while a softer one could ease December hike bets.
items.title: US October CPI Preview: Inflation Growth May Slow, How Will US Stocks, Dollar and Gold React?
Gold and Silver Price Forecast: Rebound Puts $4,150 and $55 in Focus
items.summary: FXEmpire's forecast puts gold's immediate resistance at $4,150 after Monday's rebound to near $4,130, with a break above it seen opening the way toward $4,250 and $4,400; silver needs to clear $55 to head toward $60, with support at $48. A softer dollar and falling oil drove the rebound, while Tuesday's US CPI is the next test.

items.title: Gold prices may stay volatile in 2027; JPMorgan sees $6,300 an ounce
items.summary: JPMorgan sees gold reaching $6,300 an ounce in 2027, the most bullish call among major brokerages, while UBS sees $5,200 by mid-2027 and Bank of America has trimmed its 2027 average to $5,250. Brokerages still expect central-bank buying of 600-800 tonnes to support prices despite the sharp correction from January's record, with markets pricing in a further Fed rate rise in December.

items.title: Gold rebounds above $4,100 despite strong US NFP data
items.summary: Spot gold climbed back above $4,100 in early Asian trading on Monday, recovering from Friday's payrolls-driven slide, as speculation grew that Democrats who won majorities in both chambers would push to end the Iran war. The rebound came despite October payrolls rising 165,000, far above the 65,000 forecast, which lifted December Fed hike odds to about 79.6%, FXStreet reports.

items.title: Gold trades near $4,100 as focus turns to US inflation and Fed speeches
items.summary: Gold held near $4,100 on Monday, up about 1% after an intraday high of $4,134, as the dollar gave back some post-jobs-report gains. Traders now look to Tuesday's US CPI, Friday's PPI and Fed speeches for clues on a December rate rise, priced at about an 80% chance. China also extended its suspension of an extra 24% tariff on US imports by two months.

items.title: CAS weighs on NSE, BSE Q2 earnings; MCX rides gold, silver volatility
items.summary: NSE and BSE reported sequential declines in July-September earnings as trading volumes fell after the common account statement rule, while MCX benefited from gold and silver volatility, widening the earnings divide among Indian exchanges. SEBI's rollback of the CAS rule could revive trading volumes and profitability at the equity exchanges.

items.title: Gold Price Today, November 8: Precious metals tick higher on MCX during Diwali special trading session
items.summary: MCX December gold futures rose 1.2% to Rs 1,42,335 per 10 g in the Diwali Muhurat session, while silver futures edged up 0.2% to Rs 1,85,079 per kg after touching Rs 1,85,339. Spot gold held above $4,000 at about $4,071.67 an ounce and spot silver traded near $51.97.

Global gold demand hit a record $188 billion in the third quarter, the World Gold Council said, up 22% on the year even as volumes slipped 1% to 1,369 tonnes. Central banks bought 321 tonnes, up 42% and more than jewellery demand of 313 tonnes for the first time, while ETFs added 211 tonnes to a record 4,256 tonnes. Bar and coin buying fell 19% and jewellery demand 17%.
items.title: Gold Demand Hits Record As Retail Buyers Retreat

items.summary: The rupee snapped a six-session winning streak on Monday, closing at 93.9275 per dollar against 93.9050 previously, after dollar bids from state-run banks outweighed recent gains, Reuters reports. It had touched a six-month high of 93.69; lower oil and foreign inflows lent support, and Emkay Global expects the RBI to use improved inflows to rebuild FX buffers rather than allow sharp rupee gains.
items.title: Indian rupee breaks six-day winning streak on state banks' dollar bids

items.summary: Barrick Mining's Q3 net earnings rose to $1.32 billion from $1.30 billion a year earlier, as its average realised gold price climbed 23% to $4,243 an ounce, Morningstar reports. Production slipped to 816,000 ounces from 829,000 on extreme weather and delayed access to higher-grade ore; revenue rose 22% to $5.07 billion. Spot gold averaged $4,204.59 in the quarter, up 17.6% year on year.
items.title: Barrick Quarterly Earnings Benefit from Higher Prices as Production Remains On Track for Annual Target
Bullion may remain under pressure as markets track US-Iran war, inflation
items.summary: MCX gold rose about 3% on the week to near Rs 1.42 lakh per 10 g and silver about 3.15% to near Rs 1.84 lakh per kg, with COMEX gold at $4,074.9 an ounce. Analysts say US-Iran tensions, US inflation data and the Fed's next move will set the tone next week, with safe-haven buying possible if tensions flare.

items.title: Informist Poll: Gold seen with lower bias Nov; upside if peace in West Asia
items.summary: Brokerages polled by Informist see MCX gold trading Rs 1,38,000–1,49,400 per 10 g in November and COMEX gold at $3,900–$4,250 an ounce, with a lower bias but upside if West Asia peace talks progress. Brent crude fell over 16% last week to $98.32 a barrel and the 10-year US yield eased to near 4.9%, while analysts say Indian festive demand has picked up on dip buying but remains subdued.

items.title: Iran suggests blasts are not US attacks as both sides report ships hit
items.summary: Iranian media said blasts in southern Iran on Saturday evening were linked to Iranian military activity rather than US strikes, while both sides reported shipping hit in or near the Strait of Hormuz. Iran said two oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines; the US said its air force disabled a vessel in the Gulf of Oman.

items.title: Silver Price Today: $51.89 After a 5.75% Week, CPI Due 10 November, Bull $55, Bear $49
items.summary: Silver ended Friday at $51.89 an ounce, up 5.75% on the week from $49.07, its 12-month low on 30 October. FinanceFeeds puts its bull case at $55 and bear case at $49, with the US October CPI due on Tuesday 10 November the next big test.

items.title: Silver Price Forecast: Rally Faces US CPI Test After Dollar Jump
items.summary: Silver held its rebound from the $48-50 support zone after Friday's dollar rally, FXEmpire says, but a hotter-than-expected US CPI reading on Tuesday could push the dollar toward 104 and stall the recovery. A break below $48 would raise the risk of a slide to $45, while the gold-to-silver ratio's resistance at 80 is the other level to watch.

items.title: Gold sales during Dhanteras, Lakshmi Puja may cross Rs 62,000 crore
items.summary: Gold sales across India during Dhanteras and Lakshmi Puja are estimated to cross Rs 62,000 crore, the All India Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) said on Sunday, reflecting strong festive demand despite elevated prices. GJC said gold returned about 9-14% between last year's Lakshmi Puja and this November, with prices now around Rs 1.42-1.43 lakh per 10 g.

items.title: Gold Jewellery Hallmarking: Mandatory hallmarking extended to 398 districts across 26 States, UTs
items.summary: Mandatory hallmarking of gold jewellery now covers 398 districts across 26 states and Union Territories, up from 392, after the government notified a fresh amendment to the hallmarking order. All nine Delhi districts are now covered, and Uttar Pradesh leads with 41 districts.

BIS seized 2.085 kg of gold jewellery worth about Rs 3 crore in raids on 4 November at four Coimbatore shops, after finding jewellery on display without the mandatory six-digit hallmark unique identification (HUID) number. BIS is preparing legal action, and advised buyers to check the HUID and verify hallmarks on the BIS Care app.
items.title: BIS raids 4 jewellery shops in Coimbatore, seizes gold worth Rs 3 crore
Global Gold Prices Down 24% From Record. In India, It's Down 20%. Here's What Makes Up The Difference
items.summary: Spot gold closed at $4,068.71 an ounce, about 24% below its Jan 29 record of $5,379, while Delhi gold fell only about 20% from its record. NDTV Profit puts the gap down to the duty rising from 6% to 15% in May and a rupee about 2% weaker since January, plus a January premium that has since vanished. The World Gold Council expects India's demand near 650 tonnes this year, the lowest since 2020.

items.title: Silver May Rebound Faster Than Gold, Ajay Kedia Sees ₹3 Lakh By Next Diwali
items.summary: Silver has corrected sharply from its January peak of Rs 4.20 lakh per kg to around Rs 1.90 lakh, and Kedia Advisory's Ajay Kedia expects it to recover faster than gold, moving towards Rs 2.80-3 lakh by next Diwali, while cautioning that volatility will continue.

items.title: Gold near interim bottom, but World Gold Council says three conditions associated with price recovery 'already in place'
items.summary: The World Gold Council says gold may be nearing an interim bottom, with two of three historical recovery signals in place: gold about 10% below its 200-day average and a strong dollar. Speculative positioning remains elevated, so the third signal is missing. Gold closed October at $3,913, down 6.3% in the month.

items.title: ETF Gold Flows Slow In October But Remain Positive
items.summary: Global gold ETFs added a net 19 tonnes of gold worth $2.7 billion in October, taking holdings to a record 4,275 tonnes, though assets under management fell 6% to $542 billion as prices dropped. European funds led with 13.1 tonnes of inflows and Asian funds added 9.8 tonnes, while North American funds saw 4.5 tonnes of outflows.

items.title: Dhanteras sales boom or price illusion? Why Indians spent more on gold and appliances without buying much more
items.summary: Dhanteras gold sales reached about Rs 60,000 crore, up 15–20% on last year, but the quantity sold was largely flat, jewellers' body GJC told PTI, with buyers choosing lighter jewellery, 18-carat designs and smaller coins. The World Gold Council's November 3 report showed India's September-quarter jewellery consumption down 20% year on year to 99.9 tonnes even as its value rose 16%.

items.title: India's silver import window opens as coin sales halve and London stocks build
items.summary: India has opened a simplified route for silver import licences covering about 6,500 tonnes over six months, which could ease supply in the world's most price-sensitive bullion market — if buyers use the permits. Physical demand stays muted, US Mint Silver Eagle sales fell 52% in September from a year earlier, and Metals Focus expects industrial silver demand to fall 3% in 2026.
